claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:db/schema.sql` line 20: `customer_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id),`, inside `CREATE TABLE orders (` at line 18. The lesson's block (lines 18-32) still matches the tag byte for byte after this round's edits (only the prose sentence above it changed). PostgreSQL 17 ddl-constraints: a foreign key constraint requires the values to match values appearing in some row of another table.

Same extract at stage-1: `quantity       integer NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),` and `PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)`; `order_items` declares no `id` column, so the composite PK is the only key. Unchanged this round.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs`: `public async Task<Order> PlaceOrderAsync(int customerId, List<OrderItem> items)` whose FIRST statement is `if (items.Count == 0) throw new ArgumentException("an order needs at least one item");`, with `await repository.AddAsync(order);` / `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` after it. Section 4's round-3 addition "When that check fails, it throws" is exactly this statement; the inline quote in section 5 still matches character for character.

OrderService.cs @ stage-1 holds exactly one guard (`items.Count == 0`); the rest builds `new Order { ... Items = items }` and calls AddAsync/SaveChangesAsync, never reading `Quantity` or `ProductId`. OrdersController.Create only maps `i.ProductId`, `i.Quantity`, `i.UnitPriceVnd` into `OrderItem` without testing them. So both values reach the database unchecked by application code.

Re-run live this session against donhang-api:stage-1 (container up): `POST /api/v1/orders` with `{"items":[]}` and a token for anh.tran@example.com returned `400` and exactly `{"title":"Invalid request","status":400,"detail":"an order needs at least one item"}`, the string the lesson quotes in section 5.

Re-run live this session: `{"items":[{"productId":1,"quantity":0,"unitPriceVnd":10000}]}` returned `500` with `{"title":"Server error","status":500,"detail":"something went wrong"}`; donhang-api log for that request: `Npgsql.PostgresException ... SqlState: 23514 ... new row for relation "order_items" violates check constraint "order_items_quantity_check"`. So the 500 comes from the quantity CHECK, not the product FK.
claim_verdicts.source: live run 2026-09-25: curl + docker logs donhang-api

claim_verdicts.evidence: PostgreSQL 17 ddl-constraints, fetched this session: "PostgreSQL does not support CHECK constraints that reference table data other than the new or updated row being checked." and "This assumption is what justifies examining CHECK constraints only when rows are inserted or updated, and not at other times." Both section 3's definition and section 4's round-3 split sentence ("a `CHECK` never sees past the row it's testing") stay inside that.

RFC 9110 s15.3.2, verbatim from the local mirror refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt:6970: "The 201 (Created) status code indicates that the request has been fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created." Section 6's round-3 wording ("A validation failure — one of those application-level checks failing — should still return `201`…" answered by "the order was never created") and summary line 5 both stay inside that.

Read this session: DonHang.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs @ stage-1 has `catch (KeyNotFoundException ex)` -> 404, `catch (ArgumentException ex)` -> `WriteProblemAsync(context, StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest, "Invalid request", ex.Message)`, `catch (Exception ex)` -> `Status500InternalServerError, "Server error", "something went wrong"` (a literal, not ex.Message). This is exactly what section 4 now describes: type-based recognition, the exception's own message as `detail` on the 400 path, a fixed message otherwise.

issues.text: Reading Core concepts for the first time I stopped on this line. A constraint violation cannot travel to `SaveChangesAsync()`: at that point nothing has been rejected yet. What reaches `SaveChangesAsync()` unchecked is the bad value; the violation happens afterwards, inside PostgreSQL. I only got the order straight once section 4 spelled it out, and had to come back and re-read this bullet.
issues.fix: In Core concepts, change "a constraint violation that reaches `SaveChangesAsync()` unchecked" to "a bad value that reaches `SaveChangesAsync()` unchecked, so the database is the first thing to reject it".
issues.quote: raw database error — a constraint violation that reaches `SaveChangesAsync()` unchecked, surfacing as an exception the endpoint never asked about
